question: I dropped to part-time (below half-time) this semester. How long until my unsubsidized loans come due?
reference_answer: Dropping below half-time starts your six-month grace period on Direct Subsidized and Unsubsidized Loans, unless you've already used it. Repayment begins after the grace period ends, and interest keeps accruing on unsubsidized loans in the meantime.

question: What's the smallest monthly payment someone can have on the Repayment Assistance Plan?
reference_answer: The lowest regular RAP payment is $10 a month. Borrowers with adjusted gross income of $10,000 or less have a yearly amount of $120, and any monthly payment that would be below $10 is set at $10.

question: Under the tiered standard plan, how many years would someone with a $60,000 balance get?
reference_answer: A $60,000 balance falls in the $50,000 to under $100,000 tier, so the Tiered Standard plan term is 20 years.

question: My first federal loan disburses in August 2026. Can I pick income-based repayment (IBR) when I graduate?
reference_answer: No. Loans made on or after July 1, 2026 can't be repaid under IBR, PAYE or ICR. They can be repaid under the Tiered Standard plan or the Repayment Assistance Plan (RAP).

question: How many days of missed payments before a federal Direct Loan is considered in default?
reference_answer: A Direct Loan goes into default after payments haven't been made for 270 days. Missing even one payment makes the loan delinquent, so contact your servicer as soon as you fall behind.

sources.title: Student Loan Repayment Checklist (Federal Student Aid, PDF)

question: What does a loan rehabilitation agreement require me to pay, and for how long?
reference_answer: You make nine voluntary, reasonable and affordable monthly payments, each within 20 days of the due date, over 10 consecutive months. The payment is based on your income. Afterward the loan returns to regular repayment and the default is removed from your credit history.

question: Got a notice that SAVE is ending. If I don't respond in time, which plan do I end up on?
reference_answer: If you don't choose a new plan within the at least 90-day window your servicer gives you, the Department says you'll be automatically placed in the Standard Repayment Plan or the Tiered Standard plan. You can choose an income-driven plan or RAP before then.

sources.title: U.S. Department of Education Announces Next Steps for Borrowers Enrolled in the Unlawful SAVE Plan

question: Advisor here: what's the cutoff for borrowers still on PAYE or ICR to pick a different plan, and what's the fallback?
reference_answer: Borrowers repaying under PAYE or ICR must choose another plan before July 1, 2028. If they don't, loans eligible for RAP are placed in RAP and the remaining loans go to IBR.

question: If I borrow in fall 2027 and can't find a job afterward, will an unemployment deferment be an option?
must_not_include: three more years of unemployment deferment
reference_answer: No. Unemployment and economic hardship deferments aren't available for loans disbursed on or after July 1, 2027. Borrowers with those loans can look at RAP for a lower, income-based payment, or forbearance for short-term hardship.

question: On a subsidized loan, which is better for interest: deferment or forbearance?
reference_answer: Deferment is usually better for a subsidized loan, because you generally aren't charged interest on Direct Subsidized Loans during deferment. During forbearance, interest accrues on all loans, including subsidized ones.

question: How many payments does PSLF require, and does the job have to be full-time?
reference_answer: PSLF requires 120 qualifying monthly payments on Direct Loans while working full-time, generally averaging at least 30 hours a week, for a qualifying employer such as a government agency or a 501(c)(3) nonprofit.

question: Can a parent borrower put a Parent PLUS loan on the Repayment Assistance Plan?
must_not_include: Parent PLUS loans are eligible for RAP
Parent PLUS loans can be repaid under RAP
reference_answer: No. Parent PLUS loans, and consolidation loans that repaid a parent PLUS loan, are excluded from RAP. A Parent PLUS loan made on or after July 1, 2026 is repaid under the Tiered Standard plan.

question: Where can I look up all my federal loans and see which company services them?
must_not_include: credit report is the only way
reference_answer: Log in to your StudentAid.gov account. It shows each federal loan's balance, interest rate, type and servicer. Your servicer handles payments and plan changes for free.

sources.title: Student Loan Repayment Checklist (Federal Student Aid, PDF)
sources.section: Find your loans and your servicer

question: How much does each kid I claim on my taxes knock off my RAP payment?
reference_answer: RAP reduces your monthly payment by $50 for each dependent you claimed on your federal tax return, after the payment is calculated as a percentage of your adjusted gross income. The payment can't go below $10.

question: I withdrew from my program four months before the school closed. Could closed school discharge still apply?
must_not_include: only if you were enrolled on the day it closed
reference_answer: Possibly. Closed school discharge can cover borrowers who were enrolled when the school closed or who withdrew no more than 180 days before it closed, as long as they didn't complete the program at another location or through a teach-out. Four months is inside that window, but the Department decides; apply through StudentAid.gov.
